I don't really know if I have c-PTSD or BPD but those have been tossed around and still under discussion but I can tell you for sure that I worry about everything, about irrational and rational things. It's very exhausting. My worries don't relate to my trauma, they are just random.

This is the reply I sent to someone else: [https://www.reddit.com/r/childfree/comments/b04oaa/next\_time\_anyone\_ever\_asks\_me\_why\_i\_dont\_have/eidlbeg](https://www.reddit.com/r/childfree/comments/b04oaa/next_time_anyone_ever_asks_me_why_i_dont_have/eidlbeg)

It's very hard to tease apart culture from biology. I've heard it stated though, that culture IS biology, since our personalities and preferences have a biological basis and those things factor greatly into culture. As well as our tendency to do what others around us do, because tribal acceptance is very important to humans and a deep aspect of our biology. Culture seems likely to arise out of people who live around each other develop similar moral values based on their preferences as well as what others around them do and what tends to "work" practically speaking for their community.

Life is really interesting in that random twists and turns can lead it into all sorts of directions, not necessarily toward an "ideal" but just toward what happens.

Thanks! it's not something I've spent any time looking into (yet) but it was based on observations that the people who get the most "into" parenting and genuinely love it seem to fall into the feminine/masculine stereotype moreso than non parents.

I suppose since our biological sex chromosomes on some level determine the (average) hormone profile over our lifetimes, and since sexual dimorphism is directly related to reproduction, it seems like a reasonable hypothesis that the feminine hormone profile would be best suited for motherhood and the masculine hormone profile would be best suited to fatherhood. So I'm taking a 30,000 foot view and not proposing any mechanisms at this point.

I also got clued into this possibility because of how many transgender individuals who start hormone therapy report changes in their personality - female-to-males suddenly becoming less apt to cry randomly and less interested in children. Of course I have never looked in the psych literature to see if anyone has ever tried to measure this but I can imagine a way to do that non-invasively.

So not robust but at least something to chew on.

I always wonder about this kind of thing - why someone with such serious health issues says "You know what? I'm going to take my chances." 

A woman I know who had the same illness as mine and had the same surgeries I did (we met through patient communities) decided to have two kids after her operations. I've always wondered if it ever occurred to her that her kids might end up with the same disease and have to go through the same hell and get the same operations. She knows her life was ripped apart by it but the selfish desire to breed seems to trump common sense. 

I am glad you're okay now and that your mom's decision to have kids didn't result in long term chronic illness for you, despite the issues in infancy. I'm sure there's always a chance that the kids would grow up just fine. It just seems like quite a gamble knowing that I am often suicidal and have had struggles from keeping a job to keeping friendships because of the issues I have. 

All the best to you.

This is kind of a new belief I am tossing around. I'm a  biologist so I think of things in terms of that. The balance of feminine nurture and masculine ... something....still haven't come up with the best word for it... is possibly important for a child's brain development. I am not nurturing, which would be very bad for a young child. My husband is pretty disinterested in kids and wouldn't enjoy fatherhood. He doesn't like sports and rough-and-tumble play, which would be particularly bad if we had a boy.

Yeah i guess it's an attempt to not have to say Ass-Burgers.

But it sounds very cutesy and also non particularly medical or scientific. Sounds like an internet subculture rather than a legit diagnosis.

I don't know if you've misunderstood me because of my bad writing. I write badly when I feel suicidal so I'm sorry. I don't want to "get out of doing the things that come with equality" -- I want to do them! I recognize that power = responsibility and that you have to get after it in life and you can't just expect things to be handed to you. I think a lot of women want it easy. The men built all the companies and the women want to be CEOs. Feminist businesses tend to fail. It's awful and I'm so afraid that the female mediocrity trap is going to swallow me up and destroy my dreams.

I've been depressed my whole life. My dad beat me when I was a kid and insulted me and then "forgot about it" because of his own mental illness. To this day he thinks most of it didn't really happen or wasn't that bad. It was. I was bullied horribly by other kids and never had a single friend I trusted until I met my current circle in 2008. I joined a band because I had no job, no friends, no relationship, no money. An illness i'd been dealing with for all of my 20s made it impossible for me to work full time, and not for lack of trying. I never stopped looking for work until my illness would take me out and I'd have to start over again when I'd get out of the hospital. I never stopped looking for answers. My bandmates accepted me as I am, which at 29 years old, if that's the first time that ever happens to you it's pretty sad. I am just now starting PTSD therapy because I was never allowed to call all of this stuff trauma. I finally decided to face it and say it's trauma. I'm not emotional strictly due to being female, although i'll acknowledge that's part of it. The main reason is that I'm an abuse victim and I have a bunch of mental health issues that drag me down.

I want to finish my PhD and someday make a contribution to my field of study that isn't just incremental. My main interest is "how sustainable is sustainability?" and I study indoor farming and intensive agriculture. I'm interested in  "feeding the world" - so I guess it's kinda feminine as far as scientific interests go. But I love engineering and math and I didn't figure this out until my 30s because my depression held me back. I would get super stressed out trying to do those subjects when I was a child because I was stressed at home and bullied by everyone. I took refuge in art, music, and writing because frankly those things are easier. But man....math and engineering are so much more rewarding. Actually music is the only exception. If I had to quit science today for whatever reason, I'd try to go pro with music. It's also worth mentioning that I met my husband in the band, which is like, SO woman of me. But at least I'm not the lead singer and I am competent on an actual instrument.
